Difficult Conversations & Professional Tone

Spiraling back

This topic revisits grammar you met earlier, in a harder context: Topic 7, Topic 9.

1

Essential Question

How can I communicate professionally when the patient or coworker is upset?

2

Teaching & Learning Concepts

The communication principles, workplace expectations, and healthcare context behind this topic.

  • Tone under pressure, in writing where you cannot soften it with your voice
  • De-escalation — acknowledging the feeling before addressing the facts
  • Empathy without overpromising: 'I understand' does not mean 'I will fix it'
  • Respectful language when you are being blamed
  • Boundaries: what you can offer and what you cannot
  • Professional responses to complaints
3

Grammar Focus

A small set of high-value grammar skills, tied directly to this topic's communication task.

Word choice

  • Connotation — words that mean nearly the same thing and land very differently
  • Polite requests versus commands
  • Modal verbs: could, would, may, and how they soften without hedging
  • Positive versus negative framing of the same fact
  • Avoiding judgmental language when you are frustrated

5

Formative Practice

Guided activities and short exercises. None of this is graded — it is here so you can find out what you know before it counts.

Tone under pressure

Each of these is a reply to an upset patient or coworker. Place it, then rewrite the ones that miss.

Blunt

Reads as cold or accusing

Abrupt

Correct but curt

Professional

Warm, clear, and appropriate

Over-soft

So hedged the message is lost

  • 1

    As I already explained in my previous message, the policy has not changed and there is nothing further I can do.

    BluntAbruptProfessionalOver-soft
  • 2

    Received. Will look into it.

    BluntAbruptProfessionalOver-soft
  • 3

    I am sorry you waited so long today — an hour is a long time and you were not told why. Here is what happened, and here is what I can do about the rescheduling.

    BluntAbruptProfessionalOver-soft
  • 4

    I am so incredibly sorry, this is entirely our fault and completely unacceptable, and I promise you this will never happen again and I will personally make sure everything is fixed for you.

    BluntAbruptProfessionalOver-soft

6

Cumulative Workplace Product

Combine this topic's grammar, vocabulary, and communication skills into something you would actually produce at work.

Professional response to a difficult scenario

Write a professional response to an upset patient or coworker. Acknowledge the feeling, state the facts accurately, say what you can do and what you cannot, and give a next step. Do not overpromise.

Submit through Brightspace. This page is for drafting and self-checking.

7

Revision & Reflection

Review your work against the Communication Check, then name one thing to improve next time.

Communication Check — check each criterion your writing meets

Think about

  • Read your first sentence. Does it acknowledge, or defend?
  • Did you promise anything you cannot personally deliver?
  • Would you be comfortable if your supervisor read this?
